# MeTTa from C

> A C program boots the engine in its own process, builds terms, asks, and
> reads answers back as `term_t` directly. This is the only host inside the
> engine's process, so there is no wire and no serialisation. This file is how
> to USE the seat; the repository root's llms.txt covers everything else.

## Build

```sh
sh extensions/cmetta/build.sh
```

Produces `extensions/cmetta/libcmetta.so`. Include `extensions/cmetta/cmetta.h`.

## Shape of a program

```c
#define MT_SHORTHAND               /* opt in to S() V() T() E() */
#include <cmetta.h>

metta *m = mt_open(NULL);          /* NULL on failure; mt_errmsg() says why */

mt_each (a, mt_run(m, "!(+ 1 2)"))
    printf("%s\n", mt_show(a));    /* the loop closes the cursor, break included */

int64_t n = mt_one_int(mt_eval(m, E("+", 1, 2)));
mt_close(m);
```

`mt_eval` computes at most one answer per step, so a host that wants the
first answer of many pays for one. `mt_each` opens, walks and closes;
`mt_rows (row, ...)` binds an `mt_row` instead of the atom alone, carrying
`row->atom`, `row->text` (the engine's own rendering), `row->group` and the
cursor, so `mt_bound(row, "y")` gives the binding under the name you wrote
rather than a child index. `mt_do(m, src)` runs for effect and
discards the answers.

## Five rules, and then you know the library

1. `const mt_atom *` BORROWS, non-`const` TAKES. Every door you hand a fresh
   term to takes it, so `mt_add(kb, E("edge", "a", "b"))` leaks nothing;
   `mt_keep(t)` is how you pass one you are keeping.
2. Errors are `errno`-shaped: set on failure, not cleared on success. Check a
   run once with `mt_ok()` after `mt_clear()`, not once per call.
3. One verb, either receiver. `mt_add/del/eval/match/atoms/count/wipe` take
   a `metta *` (its `&self`) or a `mt_space *`; `_Generic` picks.
4. A Number splits into INT, FLOAT, BIGINT and RATIONAL. Reading promotes where
   it is lossless (`mt_float` of an Int) and refuses where it is not
   (`mt_int` of a Float; an Int past 2^53 as a double).
5. A bare C string in term position is a SYMBOL. Text is `mt_text("...")`.

## Building terms

```c
mt_expr("+", 1, 2)                     /* (+ 1 2)       */
mt_expr("edge", "a", mt_var("y"))      /* (edge a $y)   */
mt_expr("f", mt_expr("g", 1), 2.5)     /* (f (g 1) 2.5) */
```

No count, and no constructor per child: `_Generic` reads each argument's C
type. `S() V() T() N() R() B() E()` are the same builders under
`MT_SHORTHAND`.

## Taking one answer

`mt_one(r)` is exactly one and refuses zero or many; `mt_first(r)` takes
the first and claims nothing; `mt_one_int/_float/_truth/_name(r)` give the
value with no atom to look after; `mt_all(r)` gives every answer as an `mt_list`. Each
consumes the cursor.

`mt_show`/`mt_show_dup` return presentation text. `mt_write_dup` returns an
owned counted `mt_string` that `mt_parsen(data, len)` reads back exactly; free
`data` with `mt_free`. Strict writing refuses values with no source spelling.

## Calling back into C

```c
mt_def(m, (mt_op){ .name = "hypot", .arity = 2,
                   .effect = MT_PURE, .fn = op_hypot });
```

Designated initializers name each field at the call site. `word_count`
publishes as `word-count`. Inside the function: `mt_arg`, `mt_answer`,
`mt_fail`.

## Lowering

`mt_def` publishes a C function the engine calls, and it must name an effect
class because the engine cannot see into it. `mt_lower` installs an EQUATION
from C tokens, which the engine reads, specialises and can match on:

```c
mt_lower(m, (twice $x), (* 2 $x));
mt_lower(m, (fib $n), (if (< $n 2) $n (+ (fib (- $n 1)) (fib (- $n 2)))));
```

`#` is C's compile-time access to its own source, which is what Python's
`__code__` and Node's `toString()` are at run time. Parameterise a body by its
operators and it expands to C in one mode and MeTTa in the other, so one
function is callable from both. See `examples/lower.c`.
Ordinary `mt_lower` expands C macros in its MeTTa tokens. Use `mt_lower_raw`
or `MT_METTA_RAW` when a MeTTa symbol must retain a spelling that collides with
a C macro.

## Errors, bounds and threads

`mt_error()` is the last status, `mt_errmsg()` its words. `mt_limit()`
bounds an evaluation and a bound reports `MT_LIMIT`, which is not a fault. A
thread that did not open the engine calls `mt_thread_attach()`.

## Measuring

`mt_stats_now()` twice with `mt_stats_since()` between reads the engine's
own counters around a region, which is how a C host measures without guessing.

## Where to read next

- `extensions/cmetta/cmetta.h` is the contract, and it documents each call.
- `extensions/cmetta/examples/` are runnable programs: hello, ops, stream, lower.
- The site publishes the seat's README at `/extensions/cmetta`.
